ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.49 to the rider's original payment method; send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route compliance record (no formal warning, first such incident); record a driver violation for the unexempt off-route km since there is no traffic reason (RD-2/RD-4). No account flag: RD-6's repeat condition is not met.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 30.9 km against a 20.6 km optimal route, a deviation of 10.31 km [F1], far over RD-1's 1 km tolerance, and the fare record prices that excess at $1.4100/km, excess distance billed $14.54 [F5][F7]. So a refund of the excess distance fare is due unless km are exempt under RD-3 or RD-5 [RD-2].

Segment F3 (22:54–23:03, +5.71 km) [F3]: at 22:50, before the segment began, the driver asked "Jam ahead, can go via Upper Bukit Timah Road?" [F8] and the rider answered "ok" at 22:51 [F9]. The chat is complete and every message timestamped [F10]. That is a specific named road, agreed before the segment, and UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD is among the roads this segment drove [F3], so the agreement covers the whole segment (the roads before and after the named road are part of going via it) — finding exempt, ground named_road_tied, 5.71 km exempt [RD-5].

Segment F4 (23:07–23:13, +4.73 km) [F4]: the only rider message before it is the 22:51 "ok" to a road it never drove — it ran ARCADIA ROAD → ADAM ROAD → LORNIE HIGHWAY → LORNIE ROAD → KHEAM HOCK ROAD → TREVOSE CRESCENT → MERRYN ROAD [F4][F9][F8]. The driver's "She agreed to my route" is a post-trip statement, not rider consent given before the segment [F11][RD-5]. No rider message before 23:07 agrees to this route — finding counts, ground consent_after_or_none, 4.73 km refundable [RD-5].

No traffic reason for either segment: band 8 (70+ km/h) on the BKE and PIE, no incidents near the route, fair weather [F12][F13][F14][F15], and the trace marks RD-4 ✗ for both segments [F3][F4]; the driver's "Jam ahead" therefore exempts nothing and a driver violation is recorded [RD-2][RD-4].

Arithmetic: (10.31 km deviation − 5.71 km exempt) × $1.4100/km = 4.60 × $1.4100 = $6.4860 → $6.49 [F5][RD-2]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded; surge was 1.0× [F6][F7]. Under TH-1/TH-2 a deviation under $10 is decided by the system per DISP-001, and the record is complete (GPS distance, full timed chat, statement) [F10][F7].

RD-6 does not flag the account: the driver has 1 upheld dispute in 90 days but route disputes upheld = 0 [F17], so there is no prior upheld deviation. The rider's 2 disputes, 0 upheld, and the driver's rating/trips [F16][F17] are profile facts and decide nothing.

RD-7 applies: the rider was not informed for the 23:07–23:13 stretch, so the driver gets the notification-duty reminder and the failure is logged; this is a first notification-related incident, so no formal warning [RD-7][F4].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the driver's statement and both chat messages; "I want the whole extra distance refunded" and "She agreed to my route" are about the fare and the route, and nothing describes threats, harassment, inappropriate conduct or dangerous driving — none [F8][F9][F11].

The only rider message before 23:07 is the 22:51 'ok' to UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD, which this segment did not drive (ARCADIA ROAD → ADAM ROAD → LORNIE HIGHWAY → LORNIE ROAD → KHEAM HOCK ROAD → TREVOSE CRESCENT → MERRYN ROAD) [F4][F8][F9]; the driver's post-trip statement 'She agreed to my route' is a claim, not rider consent before the deviation [F11][RD-5]. No prior agreement → counts under RD-5, 4.73 km refundable under RD-2.

element_findings.reason: Rider message 'ok' at 22:51, sent before the 22:54 segment start [F8][F9][F10], agrees to the driver's named road UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD, which F3 drove [F3] — notice and consent satisfied under RD-5.
The rider named the route via UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD by accepting the driver's proposal and the car went there [F8][F9][F3]; the segment is not a deviation under RD-3/RD-5.

The only pre-segment rider message is the 22:51 'ok' to UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD [F9], a road F4 did not drive [F4], and the driver's post-trip statement is not consent [F11] — no notice or agreement before the 23:07 segment under RD-5.
No rider message before the segment named any place or route on F4's course [F8][F9][F4]; the rider asked for no stop or route here, so RD-3 exempts nothing.

Reading the chat, statement and complaint in context, there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, inappropriate conduct or dangerous-driving allegation — the messages are about the route and the fare [F8][F9][F11]; no escalation under SAFE-1.

rejected_claims.reason: Wrongly exempts the entire 5.71 km of F3 as if consent to a named road excused more than that segment; the exemption under RD-5 is confined to the segment whose roads include the agreed road, and the arithmetic of the trace yields $6.49, not the 4.60 km result being used differently by the driver side. F3 is exempt in full (rider agreed to UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD, which F3 drove [F3][F9]) and F4 counts, so the refundable km is 10.31 − 5.71 = 4.60 and the refund $6.49, not $6.49 on a different basis [RD-5][RD-2].

Claims no part of the deviation is exempt and seeks $14.54: the rider's own 'ok' at 22:51 before the F3 segment [F9][F8] ties the named road UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD to F3 [F3], so F3's 5.71 km are exempt under RD-5 and the deviation to refund is 4.60 km, not 10.31 km [RD-5][RD-2].

RD-6 requires an upheld deviation in the last 90 days, and the driver's record shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F17]; the single upheld dispute was not a route deviation, so no flag_account follows [RD-6].

The 'no notice for the whole route' reading overstates: notice was given and agreed before F3, so RD-7's reminder and log attach only to the uninformed 23:07–23:13 stretch [F8][F9][F4], and the refund amount is fixed by the exempt-km calculation, not by the notice failure [RD-7][RD-2].

Reaches $6.49 by exempting all of F3, which is correct in result but rests on a claim that F3's exemption flows from the RD-5 road test; that is the same calculation the ruling adopts only after applying RD-2's formula (10.31 − 5.71) × $1.4100 [F3][F5][RD-2], so the figure is accepted but not the reasoning that the amount is a matter of the driver's concession.
